simple.meaning: נְאָקָה (nᵉʼâqâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a groan.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 2:24. The surrounding context includes family line, covenant, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְאָקָה (H5009) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נְאָקָה (nᵉʼâqâh) / H5009 is traced through Exodus 2:24, Exodus 6:5, Judges 2:18, Ezekiel 30:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

timeline.evidenceText: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant.

When Yahweh raised up judges for them, then Yahweh was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for it grieved Yahweh because of their groaning by reason of those who oppressed them and troubled them.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and put my sword in his hand; but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before the king of Babylon with the groaning of a mortally wounded man.
